newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Nikko unit sees no need for merger.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Nikko unit sees no need for merger.

text.p: An investment advisory unit of Japan's Nikko Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday that a healthy expansion in its managed assets left little need for the company to merge with any investment trust firms, despite the increasing number of mergers in the industry.

"Clients often ask us whether we plan to merge with any investment trust firm, but we are not considering any such things at all," Nikko International Capital Management Co Ltd president Takao Nakanishi told Reuters in an interview.
Nakanishi said he saw no merits from such a merger, as his company's managed assets have already grown steadily to 2.3 trillion yen, posting a 60 percent growth in the past year.

Nikko International Capital Management is the nation's second-largest investment advisory company in terms of the scale of its managed assets, next to an investment advisory unit of Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

"We are in no need of merging with any investment trust firm. There would be no merits from such a merger," Nakanishi said, when asked about the recent trend in the financial industry to merge investment management units.
Three investment management firms in the Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd said earlier in March that they would merge on October 1, following similar merger in the Nomura Securities group.
The moves were aimed at coping with competition in the run-up to Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation.
At present, investment advisory units of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages are not allowed to do investment trust operations unless they merge with investment trust firms.
Investment trust business, however, could be attractive if Japan allows to introduce the wrap account system, he added.

The system, used in the United States, allows a brokerage to manage investors' assets based on discretionary management contracts or the introduction of third party advisory firms to investors. Investors pay commission for advice, stock tradings and account management to the brokerage as a package.
Nakanishi said he strongly hopes the ministry will soon free up investments of the part of employees pension funds which the ministry currently directly manages.
By allowing private firms to manage the sum, worth 110 trillion yen, pension funds could enjoy higher investment returns than at present, he said. -- Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
